articles.title_orig: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
articles.title_zh: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
articles.content_orig:
Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.
Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.
Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.
There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.
Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.
"The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.
She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".
The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.
A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".
"But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.
Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".
"It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.
But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.
He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected had been received and was being acted on.
Cyber-security lecturer Rory Hopcraft told the BBC the government needed to make sure that its own infrastructure was up-to-date.
"Hacking has been around for many years," he said.
"The government are the ones who set the rules for other organisations... they just need to effectively be practising what they're preaching at this point."
Dean Presley, who has a garage in Chepstow, South Wales, told BBC Your Voice he had been unable to properly process MOTs online.
He said his computer system had been down since Wednesday morning, and while he has experienced outages before, they have not lasted this long.
"MOTs can be conducted and they're legal but none of the paperwork and certificates can be printed and they're not on the system," Dean said.
He said this has forced him to write everything on paper documents, leading to delays for customers.
PHP stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor.
It's a programming language which runs on a web server, behind the scenes of a website, and effectively lets you see the sites you visit.
When you go to a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.
It was developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, but still powers lots of platforms today.
PHP has been used across a wide range of platforms including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites - as well as to write tools to build web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.
According to cyber-security firm Wiz , which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.
And it said the flaws - now coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, affecting many past versions of it.
The PHP Foundation, the non-profit which maintains the programming language, warned this meant that, under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker would be able to remotely execute code on servers running PHP.
Some large organisations said they had seen a high volume of attempts to breach their systems.
Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, wrote on X on Thursday that the company saw "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.
"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he added.
Amazon also says it saw hackers attempt to exploit the flaws, but its websites were operating as normal.
While the impact of the PHP flaw remains to be seen, disruption continued for businesses and organisations after many sites were taken down on Wednesday.
The website of a Dutch agency specialising in cyber-security, Finland's government and parts of Wikipedia, taken temporarily offline, had returned to business as usual by Thursday.
But a number of sites appeared to have been taken offline on Thursday, as operators rushed to check if PHP might be running within their systems or if any patches were required.
In France, telecommunications company Orange also said it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.
According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally.
"The window to respond has shrunk dramatically," said Matt Hull, VP of cyber intelligence and response at global cyber security company NCC Group.
"A few years ago, attackers might have taken weeks to exploit a vulnerability. Now, it can be days or hours."
Hull also highlighted the extent of the task facing developers and engineers working to deal with the issue.
"Several days into this incident, security professionals might already be dealing with significant burnout," he said, urging a need to "make time to rest, share the workload and look after each other".
"Resilience depends on people as much as technology."

articles.content_orig:
New feature development for the innovative web browser ended last year. Now, The Browser Company is telling users to try Dia, Arc’s replacement.
New feature development for the innovative web browser ended last year. Now, The Browser Company is telling users to try Dia, Arc’s replacement.
The Browser Company plans to “sunset” its Arc browser on December 22nd, according to a post on the Arc website . The company moved on to developing its AI-focused Dia browser last year, but it had continued to maintain Arc. Now, the innovative browser will be going away for good.
The shutdown is happening in a few stages. Starting today, you can’t make new Arc accounts. On November 23rd, on iOS and Android, the Browse for Me and “other AI features” will be disabled and “you will no longer be able to sign in or sync your tabs.” On December 22nd, the Arc browser won’t be accessible on macOS or Windows, Arc accounts will be deactivated, and Arc Search for Android will be removed from Google Play.
The Browser Company has an FAQ about how to import your data into Dia, if you want to move to that browser. Dia is now where the company is focused, “including our whole security team.”
Arc, which had a lot of big ideas about browsers that have popped up in other browsers since. The Zen browser, which is based on Mozilla’s Gecko engine, is a frequent recommendation for people looking for an Arc-like experience. Last year, Atlassian acquired The Browser Company for $610 million .

articles.title_orig: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
articles.title_zh: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
articles.content_orig:
Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, are exposed to two publicly reported remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative , with no fix yet in the mainline kernel.
One of them, ZDI-CAN-33774, can be triggered before any network authentication. The other, ZDI-CAN-33549, requires the SMB Direct transport and an RDMA-capable network interface.
ZDI-CAN-33549 is an integer underflow in KSMBD's SMB Direct path. A client can supply RDMA buffer descriptors in which the first is longer than the declared payload, causing the server's size counter to wrap and allowing a subsequent memory copy to overrun the end of an allocated buffer.
It requires three things: an RDMA-capable interface (hardware or the rxe software driver), a writable KSMBD share, and a client negotiating SMB Direct.
ZDI-CAN-33774 requires no authentication, exposing any server running KSMBD on port 445. The flaw is a race in how KSMBD assigns its handler table: a burst of short SMB1 packets followed by an SMB2 packet in the same TCP write causes workers to handle SMB1 data with an SMB2 handler, reading past the end of the shorter buffer. A path to writing past the buffer also exists once an attacker has access to a share.
As of Thursday, neither flaw has a named fix in the mainline kernel or in linux-next , the integration tree that feeds it. Linux news site Phoronix said SMB Direct maintainer Stefan Metzmacher submitted a fix for ZDI-CAN-33549 targeting the next kernel development cycle, but this has not been confirmed elsewhere.
Fixes to mainline typically take weeks to reach stable branches and distribution kernels after that. Neither flaw has a CVE identifier, since the kernel project assigns those only after a stable-tree fix is available.
Running systemctl status ksmbd or lsmod | grep ksmbd confirms whether the module is active. Red Hat Enterprise Linux does not include KSMBD by default, according to Red Hat's support documentation .
The ZDI reports credit TrendAI, Trend Micro's AI scanner, as the finder. The Linux kernel's security documentation , updated in May 2026 following guidance from Linus Torvalds , states that bugs found by AI tools are, by definition, already public and should be sent to subsystem developer lists.
ZDI's routing appeared to follow that logic, copying public mailing lists alongside the private kernel security address without attaching patches to any of the reports.
Stable-kernel maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman replied to three of the five kernel reports within minutes of each other. To the report on the VMware GPU driver , he wrote: "For some reason you sent this to public lists, and did not include a patch, so there's not much we can do with this." On the NVMe driver report , seventeen seconds later: "Again, no patch, and sent to a public list? Please fix your submission process."
Three of the five kernel reports are not related to SMB. ZDI-CAN-33367 , discovered by researcher p1r0x , is a local privilege escalation in the kernel's networking stack that requires local access. ZDI-CAN-34068 is a local privilege escalation in the VMware virtual GPU driver, ZDI-CAN-34076 is an information disclosure in the NVMe target driver, and neither affects KSMBD servers.
A sixth ZDI report, ZDI-CAN-32005, is a buffer overflow in ConnMan , a network daemon separate from the Linux kernel.

articles.title_zh: France's Macron tightens curbs on protests, blaming hard left for unrest
articles.content_orig:

Our fall fundraising drive ends tomorrow, and we’re still $10,000 short of our goal. No billionaire owners, no paywall, no targeted ads—just readers like you. Can you chip in before time runs out?
French President Emmanuel Macron, whose popularity ratings (at around 18 percent) are well below Trump’s, exited Paris yesterday for the Middle East, even as some neighborhoods of major French cities were still smoking. Supposedly, he is on a mission to bring down fuel prices. Bonne chance to that.
The French mess is best understood in three dimensions that are all connected—the social, the economic, and the political. Socially, the protests, which caught the government by surprise in their ferocity, are mainly symptoms. The most severe riots since the famous events of 1968 began with high school students, who are ostensibly fed up with tattered schools and inadequate materials. But what they are really despairing about is the absence of life chances and hope.
Much of this protest is centered in the French banlieues —the suburbs . In France, where the social meaning of suburb is the opposite of America’s, the banlieues are where the government stashed immigrants and the local poor in massive housing projects that are bleak social failures, while the affluent live in chic city arrondissements .
This story first appeared in our free Today on TAP newsletter, a weekday email featuring commentary on the daily news from Prospect reporters.
No paywall, no programmatic ads — just the reporting. Unsubscribe anytime. Submitting your email signs you up for Today on TAP, our weekday afternoon newsletter.
This social failure is hardly a secret. Several recent hit French films are about seemingly unteachable insolent students and idealistic but quickly burnt-out teachers, beginning with the 2008 classic Entre Les Murs . In the popular TV series, Marseille , starring the great warhorse actor Gérard Depardieu as the mayor, kids in the housing projects do violent errands for the local Mafia.
And it isn’t just students who are disaffected. Just about everyone is pissed at one grievance or another. That’s why the protests spread. The French riots are reminiscent of the old Irish joke in which a man in a pub observes a brawl break out and inquires, “Is this a private fight or can anyone get into it?”
France’s welfare state has reached it limits to compensate for an economy that works only for the rich.
The second, and related, dimension is economic. The French economic model is failing the citizenry, and its failure is a variation of what is occurring throughout the West.
The turn to global neoliberalism since the 1980s has not increased economic performance, but widened inequality. The lackluster growth has put increased pressure on the French welfare state, which is relatively generous. But the welfare state has reached its limits to compensate for an economy that works only for the rich.
As French deficits and debts have increased, the global bond market has raised government borrowing costs, exacerbating the fiscal stress. Interestingly, it is considered a crisis that the French ten-year government bond just hit an interest rate of 5 percent . In the U.S., the ten-year bond sailed past 5 percent weeks ago. But France, as a medium-sized economy, is more dependent on the bond market than the U.S. is.
Macron, the ultimate in technocratic leaders, has tried to trim costs, most recently with a 43 billion euro cut in public spending in his proposed 2026-2027 budget, which includes an increase in the retirement age and cuts in health and other social spending. But these proposed cuts, which are unlikely to be enacted, have only made him more detested.
Politically, these multiple crises, punctuated by protests that in places turned violent, demonstrated the collapse of the political center, and energized the far left and especially the far right. With presidential elections set for April 2027, in two rounds, Marine Le Pen of the Rassemblement National (National Rally) is the front-runner . On the far left, Jean-Luc Mélenchon of La France Insoumise (France Unbowed) cheered on the protests.
Polls show Mélenchon running second, well behind Le Pen. If the final round is Le Pen versus Mélenchon, Le Pen almost certainly wins and by a wide margin. Other candidates on the moderate left and moderate right splinter the rest of the vote.
One outside chance of denying the presidency to Le Pen would be if Raphaël Glucksmann, the nominee of the Socialist Party, continues to gain ground and edges out Mélenchon to face Le Pen in the final round. The latest polls show Le Pen at 36 percent, Mélenchon with 16.5 percent, and Glucksmann 13.5 percent. On the center-right, former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe draws about the same share as Glucksmann.
While the far-left Mélenchon could not defeat Le Pen in the final, Glucksmann or Philippe might well do it. But for that to happen, one would have to withdraw and throw their support to the other—a most un-French sacrifice for the greater good.
The French gains for the far left and the far right are a variant of what is occurring all over Europe, as the center has utterly failed to deliver prosperity and opportunity to ordinary working people and cultural issues have backfired on the socially tolerant moderate left.
In The New York Times, the estimable Steven Erlanger has a smart explainer piece on this dynamic. Complementing his own excellent analysis, Erlanger quotes the Nobel laureate MIT economist Daron Acemoglu pointing out that the traditional moderate left got sidetracked with elite cultural issues and ignored its working-class base. “The centerpiece has to be creating jobs and wage growth and career paths for people without college degrees and diverse skills,” Acemoglu told Erlanger in an interview.
As we used to say in my grade school, No shit, Dick Tracy. I can’t resist adding that when writers in The American Prospect , or our friends at the Economic Policy Institute, keep pointing this out (over decades), it’s not a story. When a prominent mainstream economist finally figures it out, it’s worth a Nobel.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio thanked Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister for the country's help in the region in a call on Thursday.
Rubio "reaffirmed the United States' commitment to Qatar's security and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz."
"The Secretary also expressed appreciation for Qatar's continued mediation efforts and strong and close partnership in promoting a more secure region," the State Department said.
In a readout from the Qatari side, they said the two sides discussed de-escalating tensions, while confirming it supported "endeavors aimed at reaching a solution that ensures freedom of maritime navigation and paves the way for a comprehensive agreement that achieves lasting peace in the region."
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are having only a "limited" economic impact on the kingdom so far, owing to robust domestic demand, the International Monetary Fund's regional director told AFP, though geopolitical uncertainty remains a threat.
The Iranian-backed Yemeni group has ramped up its attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, hitting oil facilities and airports among other targets, as Yemen's dormant civil war has roared back into life.
Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, has had its crude shipments squeezed by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis' declaration of a maritime blockade.
But shipments continue to move despite the conflicts, Jihad Azour, the regional director, told AFP.
The Gulf kingdom also has "strong internal demand and a robust public sector, so the impact is limited," he said of the Houthi attacks.
Nevertheless, the economy is expected to contract by 3.3% this year, owing to the impacts of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran that began in February. The economy of the region as a whole is expected to shrink 4.8% in 2026, the IMF said.
As oil prices crept up to their highest levels since May, President Trump accused Iran of lying about the situation in the Strait of Hormuz in order to drive up costs.
"Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social . "They are even making up fake hits, mines, and everything else, because more Oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the Conflict."
The price for Brent crude, the international standard for oil, reached $112 a barrel on Thursday morning. The cost hadn't reached at least $112 since May 18.
Iran announced they had struck four vessels in the area of the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, while three others hit sea mines. All of the damaged ships were along the southern route, hugging the Omani coast, used by the U.S. to escort tankers out of the Persian Gulf, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.
While the U.S. is escorting large amounts of oil out of the Gulf, it is a costly process. Overall instability in the region is also continuing to keep prices high despite increased supply since the early weeks of the war.
Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the group's armed forces have carried out four military operations against targets inside Saudi Arabia in the last 48 hours, including on the Defense Ministry building in Riyadh, the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an Aramco facility in Yanbu and Abha International Airport.
In a video statement published on his X account, Saree claimed the attacks were carried out using ballistic missiles and drones, with direct hits on all four targets.
"The criminal Saudi enemy has carried out, during its aggression and latest escalation over the past 100 days, more than 2,900 airstrikes and missile attacks targeting civilian objects in our beloved country," he said. "Through these attacks, it has committed dozens of crimes, leaving more than 562 people killed and wounded, the majority of them women and children."
CBS News has not independently verified the claims.
The Houthis "will continue their operations deep inside Saudi Arabia in defence of our country and our people," he added.
Anti-American propaganda is a common sight on the streets of the Iranian capital, but authorities have gone a step further with their latest effort – a life-size jail cell with an actor playing President Trump languishing inside.
The 3D art installation is proving a hit with locals, who have been stopping to take selfies as well as hurl abuse at the pseudo-Trump.
Since the ongoing war began with joint American and Israeli strikes on Feb. 28, Iran has ramped up its propaganda operations. In the new campaign, a mock-prison cell is suspended several stories high over Tajrish Square, in an upscale neighborhood of north Tehran.
The actor, wearing a prosthetic mask to look like Mr. Trump, paces around the cell or clutches its bars. A screen set up nearby shows messages denouncing alleged U.S. war crimes .
Tehran's municipal authorities, which are behind the campaign, have said the objective is to remind the capital's residents of Iran's demands for justice .
The Saudi-led coalition fighting on behalf of Yemen's government in the neighboring country's spiraling civil war said Thursday that four more drones were intercepted over the capital and the hold city of Medina.
The force did not attribute the attacks to anyone, but the drones were likely launched by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels, who have peppered Saudi Arabia with deadly strikes in recent weeks, with many projectiles getting through the kingdom's defenses .
Earlier Thursday the Saudi coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed one drone over Riyadh, again without saying where it had come from.
The Houthis have repeatedly denied targeting Medina or Mecca, the two holiest cities in Islam.
The shadow fleet of tankers holding Iran's offshore oil reserves, which it had been selling to China throughout the war against the U.S. and Israel, have run dry, intelligence firm Kpler told The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday.
The millions of barrels of crude, held on dozens of oil tankers in Asian water, ran out in mid-October, Kpler told the outlet, with a U.S. naval blockade preventing Iran from replacing the crude being sold to Chinese refineries.
"There's no more oil to discharge to China anymore," said Homayoun Falakshahi, head of crude-oil analysis at the firm.
The U.S. naval blockade has cost Iran at least $25 billion in oil revenue, according to U.S. Central Command.
Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty on Thursday said all options must be explored to find a political solution between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
At a press conference where he reiterated solidarity with Saudi Arabia, he stressed "the necessity of exploring all avenues for reaching political solutions."
The conflict between the Saudi-backed Yemeni government and the Iran-backed Houthis erupted in summer and has drastically escalated in recent weeks.
Egypt announced Sunday that it was prepared to provide military assistance to Saudi Arabia .
A spokesman for Yemen's Houthi rebels accused Saudi Arabia on Thursday of targeting an Indian yacht near Zuqar Island in the Red Sea with 14 Indian nationals on board.
In a statement published on X , Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the group's forces were carrying out rescue operations and would provide further information later.
"The Saudi enemy targets an Indian yacht near Zuqar Island, with 14 people of Indian nationality on board, according to preliminary information," he wrote in his post.
"This reckless act by the Saudi enemy in targeting the yacht threatens international navigation in the Red Sea, and the international community must stop the Saudi enemy from these reckless actions," said Saree.
There was no further information or other reports available to corroborate the Houthis' claim.

articles.title_orig: Lawsuit accuses Trump of illegally profiting off foreign crypto deals
articles.title_zh: Lawsuit accuses Trump of illegally profiting off foreign crypto deals
articles.content_orig:
A lawsuit filed Thursday accuses President Donald Trump and his family's crypto company of "corruptly profiting" off more than $2 billion in digital currency -related deals, violating constitutional restrictions on accepting foreign money.
"No president in American history has profited from his office so brazenly," alleges the federal civil complaint from a shareholder of Circle Internet Group , a publicly traded U.S. crypto company and competitor of the Trump family business, World Liberty Financial .
The suit filed in U.S. District Court in Washington by shareholder and former Circle employee J. Benjamin Greenberg centers on two allegedly "illegal foreign emoluments" involving World Liberty and Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the national security advisor to the United Arab Emirates.
Days before Trump's inauguration in January 2025, an entity backed by Tahnoon — widely known as the "Spy Sheikh" because of his powerful intelligence role — agreed to buy a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.
The company told The Wall Street Journal , which revealed the transaction in January 2026, that Trump had no involvement in the deal. But Trump would receive millions of dollars from that purchase after becoming president, according to his financial disclosures.
The lawsuit also highlights a "scheme" by an Abu Dhabi-based investment fund chaired by Tahnoon to "inflate the value of President Trump's crypto holdings" through last year's purchase of $2 billion in World Liberty's stablecoin, USD1.
The lawsuit asserts the conduct violates the U.S. Constitution's Foreign Emoluments Clause, which forbids federal officeholders from accepting money or other gifts from foreign officials without the consent of Congress.
"This is yet another frivolous lawsuit that echoes the same, tired narrative that Democrats have pushed against President Trump, his family, and his administration for a decade," White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told CNBC in a statement. "There are no conflicts of interest."
"What President Trump did is brazenly corrupt. He's made millions from these deals by selling out the American people," Matt Pelikan, an attorney at Evergreen Legal representing Greenberg, said in a statement to CNBC.
"We're suing to stop the corruption and to force President Trump to return the profits to American taxpayers," Pelikan said.
The suit says Greenberg is filing derivatively on behalf of Circle. The company said in a statement to CNBC it was not behind the lawsuit and does not comment on pending litigation. "Circle did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing," the company said via a spokesperson.
The suit names Trump, World Liberty and U.S. Middle East Special Envoy Steve Witkoff as defendants, as well as four related limited liability companies.
"World Liberty Financial is compliant with all U.S. laws and regulations," David Wachsman, a World Liberty spokesperson, told CNBC. "No one at World Liberty Financial works for the U.S. Government. These claims are without merit and we look forward to resolving them in court."
The White House and a spokesperson for Witkoff did not immediately respond to CNBC's requests for comment on the lawsuit.
In addition to seeking a court declaration that Trump's profits violate the Constitution, Greenberg wants the president to disclose all other foreign crypto emoluments he's received and return any profits found to be illegal.
Trump and his family have rapidly expanded their crypto business since he returned to the White House. World Liberty Financial, launched with members of the Trump and Witkoff families in 2024, operates the USD1 stablecoin, and an entity affiliated with Trump and his family owns about 38% of the company. The business has been highly lucrative for Trump even as WLFI investors suffered steep losses . Trump reported more than $1.4 billion in crypto income in his 2025 annual financial disclosure , including nearly $800 million tied to World Liberty. WLFI, meanwhile, fell from about 45 cents in August 2025 to about 5 cents by the end of June 2026. The venture has drawn particular scrutiny over its ties to the UAE. Months after Tahnoon's 2025 investment, the administration expanded UAE access to advanced U.S. AI chips , including for G42, a UAE state-backed AI company controlled by Tahnoon. Stocks tumbled slid on Thursday on renewed concerns around spending by artificial intelligence companies, while while oil prices jumped as geopolitical tensions rise.
The Nasdaq Composite pulled back 2.4%, while the S&P 500 shed 1.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 89 points, or 0.2%.
Meta Platforms slipped 7% even it exceeded revenue expectations and offered upbeat guidance. Technology more broadly was under pressure as well as ongoing concerns about artificial intelligence spending persisted. Advanced Micro Devices fell more than 7%, while Micron Technology and Nvidia dropped 5% and 4%, respectively.
Neocloud leader CoreWeave , whose bond yields and credit default swaps remain elevated , declined more than 9% as well. The move comes as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC Thursday that demand for neoclouds is " off the charts ." However, he added that capital is scarce and impeding growth.
Huang's commentary about a scarcity of capital is "spooking markets and reigniting the concerns around the capital markets on the credit side being full from a risk appetite standpoint," said Wells Fargo traders in a note. They also said Meta's comments about the large amount of AI funding needed caused the shares to roll over and weighed on overall market.
JPMorgan traders noted that Wednesday's bullish "tone reversed overnight" because Meta shares rolled over in the premarket and chatter increased "over renewed Iran kinetic-risk post US mid-term election."
Additionally, "underlying price actions and feedback from our trading desk also suggested the still fragile narrative around AI financing concerns and the lack of conviction/re-grossing from the recent tech reversal," they said in a note to clients.
Oil prices, meanwhile, jumped after The New York Times reported, citing sources, that the U.S. and Israel have plans for renewed strikes against Iran following next month's midterm U.S. elections. President Donald Trump also told reporters late Wednesday that Washington is not negotiating with Tehran and that something will happen "fairly soon."
International benchmark Brent crude futures traded 3% higher at above $112 per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude futures advanced 2% to above $99 per barrel.
Investors also turned to U.S. Treasurys in their search for a safe haven. The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield dropped more than 18 basis points to 4.965%, falling to its lowest level in almost a month . The 2-year note yield also shed more than 17 basis points to trade at 4.65%.
Shares of Skydance fell around 1% in afternoon trading after Tesla CEO Elon Musk made a roughly $1 billion investment in the company.
The investment comes amid a wider effort by Skydance to raise equity investments as it looks to cut costs.

Wolfe Research downgraded Netflix to peer perform from outperform.
Wolfe cited stagnant viewer engagement, intensifying streaming competition and concerns about the company's long-term growth prospects.
"Engagement failed to respond to rising investment, and last week's content leadership changes convince us that solutions require patience & lower incremental margins. Attention economy competition is rampant. Consensus estimates look fair. Downgrade to Peer Perform," Wolfe's analyst Peter Supino said.
The streaming giant has struggled, Supino said, to generate new hits despite increasing content spending by $3 billion over the past two years. The firm also removed its $95 price target.
Despite $3B of content expense growth over the last two years, "Netflix has lost its mojo" according to Supino. The analyst pointed to growing competition from YouTube and rival streaming platforms, adding  that higher programming costs may weigh on Netflix's future profit margins. Recent changes to Netflix's content leadership could help, but improvements will likely take time.
"In a not unreasonable downside scenario where Netflix revenue decelerates to MSD by 2030 (not our base case), we think NFLX would be worth ~$50/shr. today, and therefore do not think LT engagement / growth concerns are fully priced in," Supino said.
Shares of CME Group advanced 3% on the back of an upgrade by JPMorgan.
The bank re-rated the stock to overweight from underweight and increased its December 2027 price target on the stock to $367, up from their prior $250.
JPMorgan analyst Kenneth Worthington describer the current interest rate environment as "constructive" for further growth in CME's interest rate business since the company benefits when CME activity when longer term rates are rising.
He also favors CME's launch of a series of new products, which could "evolve into larger opportunities," citing its successful launch of its crypto futures service.
The analyst also cites CME's expansion in some cases to 24/7 trading for pre-existing retail-sized contracts.
Rollins reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter results as the pest control company continued to face challenges attracting residential customers.
Revenue rose 6.2% from a year earlier to $1.09 billion, while adjusted earnings came in at 33 cents per share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of 34 cents per share on revenue of $1.11 billion.
"We are disappointed with our third quarter performance and are acting with urgency to address the challenges impacting our results. We now have a clearer understanding of how the customer acquisition landscape is evolving and are taking concrete steps to optimize our approach," said President and CEO Jerry Gahlhoff Jr.
To be sure, the stock rose more than 4%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 218 points, or 0.4%. The S&P 500 shed 0.9%, and the Nasdaq Composite pulled back 1.5%.
Shares of Lockheed Martin rose more than 4% after the company reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. Driven by strong demand for fighter jets and missile defense systems, Lockheed also hiked its earnings and revenue guidance for 2026.
The company now expects 2026 ⁠sales of about $80 billion to $82 billion, up from its previous outlook of $79.75 billion to $81.75 billion.
Sales for the defense contractor touched $20.6 billion, an increase of 11% from a year earlier. Lockheed's order backlog jumped to a record $292 billion, boosted by a $52.5 billion multiyear contract for PAC-3 missile interceptors amid heightened global defense demand.
Shares of Procter & Gamble added around 3% in premarket trading after the consumer goods company posted a beat on both the top and bottom lines for its fiscal first quarter..
The Tide and Pampers parent saw adjusted earnings of $2 per share, topping the $1.88 consensus estimate, according to LSEG. Revenue came in at $23.28 billion, above the $22.80 billion expected from analysts.
Procter & Gamble also raised its full-year revenue guidance to a range of 2% and 4%, up from its prior guidance of 1% to 3%.
"While we expect there will continue to be geopolitical and economic challenges, this strong start keeps us on track to deliver within our guidance ranges for organic sales growth, core EPS growth and free cash flow productivity for the fiscal year," CEO Shailesh Jejurikar said in a statement.

articles.title_orig: How well have past GOTY winners sold?
articles.title_zh: How well have past GOTY winners sold?
articles.content_orig:
We’re less than two months away from 2026’s The Game Awards, and what a year it’s been for fantastic games, including Resident Evil Requiem , Forza Horizon 6 , Slay the Spire II , the Blood of Dawnwalker , and Control Resonant – just to name a few.
So as we approach the end of the year, we thought we’d look back on our estimates for the GOTY winners of the past four years. In terms of revenue, Elden Ring (2022 winner), Baldur’s Gate 3 (2023), Astro Bot (2024), and Expedition 33 (2025) have generated a combined $3.8B via 73M copies sold:
Elden Ring is a phenomenon in every sense. It’s sold a whopping 36.4M copies across Steam (50%), PS5 (35%), and Xbox (15% across console and PC).
Want more free estimates and insights in your inbox twice a week? Subscribe below!
Elden Ring also just passed an astronomical milestone: $2B in revenue. While PlayStation and Xbox account for half of Elden Ring ’s copies sold across these three platforms, they account for 57.5% of revenue. This – as ever – is due to regional pricing and the higher relative share of PC gamers in lower-priced markets.
For example, around 17.4% of Elden Ring ’s Steam copies sold were in China, where the game costs about 26% less than the price in the States.
There’s an … interesting narrative going around these days that console gamers are only interested in ball-and-gun games and have the patience for little else. Well, Elden Ring ’s impressive sales prove that is simply not true, and across all platforms. What’s more, over 9.8M people have played Elden Ring for over 100 hours, with nearly 3.5M people getting all of the achievements and trophies.
For reference, 10.9% of Elden Ring ’s PlayStation players have the platinum trophy, while 10.5% of players on Steam and 3.9% of Xbox players unlocked all the achievements. Git gud, Xbox players!
Of the 1.5M people who played Elden Ring on PlayStation last month, 4% also played Dark Souls 3 last month, 4% played Bloodborne , and 3% played Sekiro . There’s those Soulsborne diehards for you.
By many accounts, including my own, Elden Ring is one of the best games of all time. It’s an evergreen seller that will continue to be a cash cow for Bandai and FromSoftware for years to come.
Want more free estimates and insights in your inbox twice a week? Subscribe below!
Elden Ring has sold another 2M copies across Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox this year, generating almost $110M. This means it’s outperforming many of this year’s high-profile releases. Even Elden Ring ’s standalone run-based PvE spinoff, 2025’s Nightreign , has sold 7.8M copies and generated $282M in revenue.
Another cross-platform phenomenon is Baldur’s Gate 3 , which has sold 23.2M copies and generated over $1.2B in revenue.
About 18.7M of these copies (80.6%) are via Steam, 2.9M via PS5 (12.7%), and 1.6M (6.8%) via Xbox. Around 1.3M folks on Steam bought BG3 before it hit 1.0.
The PlayStation version launched about a month after the PC 1.0 release, while the Xbox version came four months later due to technical issues around developing local co-op on the Series S.
Want more free estimates and insights in your inbox twice a week? Subscribe below!
Across platforms, Baldur’s Gate 3 ’s monthly active users have never dropped below 2M, including 2.2M MAUs last month (68.5% on Steam, 21.9% on PS5, and 9.6% on Xbox). And it still regularly brings in 280K to 400K players every day:
About 1% of BG3 ’s Steam player base has played for over 500 hours! That’s a little under 200K people.
Astro Bot , 2024’s winner, has now sold 4.7M copies and generated $291M in revenue. The budget, including marketing, is almost certainly under $100M, given the small Japan-based core team and three-year dev timeline. You can really see why the tides are changing toward less expensive hubs.
Astro Bot is the only first-party winner on this list, but follows other first-party winners of The Last of Us Part II (2020’s winner), God of War (2018), and Breath of the Wild (2017).
Around 46.6% of Astro Bot ’s copies sold have been physical, which is far higher than the typical game. This makes sense for a couple of reasons:
There’s a large family audience for this one, and physical boxes are an item to wrap when giving Astro as a gift.
Astro has collector value for the PlayStation core (this is nostalgia-fueled platformer celebrating PlayStation’s history)
Want more free estimates and insights in your inbox twice a week? Subscribe below!
Astro is another one of those games that continues selling over time, regularly selling more than 100K a month. It’s sold around 1M more copies this year ($60M in revenue) and is a popular title with families. We can see this using the Alinea platform’s MAU crossover tool:
Astro Bot ’s top #2, #3, and #4 games by crossover in any given month this year are Minecraft , Fortnite , and Roblox – without fail.
The #1 title every month, though, is Astro’s Playroom , a pack-in with all PS5 consoles.
For every month this year, between 20% and 30% of Astro Bot players also played Astro’s Playroom that month.
So the free pack-in is a noice funnel for converting players to a full paid product.
Finally, we have last year’s winner – Expedition 33 . The turn-based-RPG banger has generated $366M via 8.7M copies sold, with 58.8% on Steam, 35.7% on PS5, and 5.5% on Xbox.
Xbox’s share of copies sold is this low due to Expedition 33 launching on Game Pass, where 4.3M people across console and PC accessed the game. A little under 700K Xbox players used their subscription to play Expedition 33 this year.
That said, the game’s 1.5-year Game Pass deal ended last week on October 16, and we’re already beginning to see a positive trend on Expedition 33’s copies sold via Xbox (but the jury’s still out!).
There’s understandably a lot of French pride behind this one, as France is the game’s #3 market on both Steam and PlayStation. Vive la France!
One thing that stood out to me is that the GOTY winners aren’t $300M Hollywood productions made in the US. They’re mostly mid-budget studios outside the traditional AAA cost centres. Lots to think about there.
Also, good games sell well; who’d have thunk it!?
And there’s a whole load of them this year, with GTA 6 still to come, too. GTA just made the cutoff point for the VGAs this year. What a coincidence!

articles.title_zh: U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Falls Under 5% as French Turmoil Fuels Flight for Safety
articles.content_orig:
Treasury yields fell sharply on Thursday, with investors turning to safe havens amid a steep sell-off in equities driven by concerns around the artificial intelligence trade and surging oil prices.
The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield — used for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — dropped more than 18 basis points to 4.965%. It marked the first time since Sept. 23 that the yield traded below 5%.
The yield on the 2-year Treasury note , which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, fell more than 17 basis points to 4.65%. The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys — which often moves on geopolitical developments — was more than 13 basis points lower at 5.30%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
The move comes as equities came under pressure after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC Thursday that while demand for neoclouds is " off the charts ," capital was scarce.
"It is a flight to safety," said Mitch Goldberg, president of ClientFirst Strategy. "People are all of a sudden terrified of the amount of bond issuance by AI-related companies. They see the rates going up and people want to hold on to something that they think will be there at maturity."
The latest slide in Treasury yields marks a turnaround from earlier this month, when both the 10-year and 30-year yields reached their highest levels in more than two decades amid investors' worries about inflation and elevated energy prices. However, attitudes have shifted as investors have found yields above 5% an attractive entry point, especially with tensions in the Middle East ramping up again.
Tensions in the region added to the session's risk-off tenor Thursday. Oil prices moved sharply higher on Thursday, with West Texas Intermediate futures edging closer to $100 a barrel. WTI was last up more than 2% at above $99 per barrel. Brent crude , the global price benchmark, increased more than 2% to above $111.
That followed a New York Times report, citing unnamed U.S. officials, that the U.S. and Israel are considering resuming strikes on Iran in a "short but intensive" operation following next month's midterms elections.

articles.title_orig: Meta strikes deal to stop Mark Zuckerberg leaving California over billionaire tax
articles.title_zh: Meta strikes deal to stop Mark Zuckerberg leaving California over billionaire tax
articles.content_orig:
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.
The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.
He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.
California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.
The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years. Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1% each year.
Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state. His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.
Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.
It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.
In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.
Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday , Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder. Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.
Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing. The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.
The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.
Meta called the deal with Zuckerberg its "Founder Alignment Agreement," saying it was "critically important" to keep him leading the company from California given the "dramatic and unprecedented transformation taking place in the tech industry and global economy related to artificial intelligence."
The company alluded to problems the company experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Zuckerberg began working outside of the office and mostly from his large compound in Kauai, Hawaii.
After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.
Layoffs have continued into this year. The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.
Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.
With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.
Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres .
Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects. The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.
It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.
And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.
The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.
Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

articles.content_orig:
Nintendo is welcoming the spooky season the only way it knows how: with a big old eShop sale, of course!
The ' Screaming Deals ' sale is now live on the North American eShop, bringing welcome discounts to a whole host of Switch 1 and 2 bangers until 31st October at 11:59 PT — so make sure you've made the most of it by then!
There are so many games on sale, in fact, that we have assembled the following list to showcase the cream of the crop, pulling every 'Screaming Deals' game we rated a 9/10 or higher (plus one personal pick from those that fell below the review bar, because we couldn't resist).

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.
We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.
Alien: Isolation is a survival horror masterpiece and straight-up one of the very best horror video games ever released.
It's a nerve-wracking affair — a slow, methodical game of cat and mouse against a brilliantly clever recreation of one of cinema's most infamous killers — but if you're up to the task you'll find one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences in the genre; a brilliant and beautiful homage to one of the greatest sci-fi movies of all time.
Feral Interactive has done a stellar job with this Switch port and the excellent motion controls and inclusion of all previously-released DLC only go to sweeten the deal. This is essential stuff for survival horror fans.
Developer Shared Memory's stated goal was “to craft complete experiences that will be playable long after the world loses its internet connection,” and screen after screen, Animal Well excels in delighting your eyes and giving your brain something to stew on.
It’s a riposte against a culture of post-launch updates in favour of a meticulously crafted, singular vision with potentially years’ worth of discoveries baked in. By all indications, Animal Well delivers on that long-term promise and does so with a one-of-a-kind elegance.
A slice of Viking strategic combat right out of the heart of Scandinavia’s indie development scene, Bad North was at the vanguard of a wave of smart yet intrinsically accessible real-time strategy titles.
Swedish developer Plausible Concept calls it ‘micro-strategy’ and it's the perfect encapsulation of a minimalist approach that covers everything from unit management to the Monument Valley -style isometric art style.
With enough enemy variance to convince you you’re playing an interactive episode of the Vikings TV show, this endlessly entertaining sea of bitesize battles will teach you to fear — and love — the sound of the oncoming horde.
Balatro is a roguelike for gamers who don't like roguelikes... and then everybody else on top of that. It utterly nails what it sets out to do, providing an instantly accessible, satisfying, and addictive gameplay loop that anybody can grasp.
It's an immensely enjoyable experience from the start, but as you get deeper in, there's really nothing else quite like it. Sublime.
It looks like The Witness and it plays a bit like StreetPass Garden , but Botany Manor blooms into something that's not only entirely its own, but also something quite special. Don't let its cosy aesthetics fool you — Botany Manor is packed with nicely challenging, well-designed puzzles, and isn't afraid to tackle heavy subjects, too.
As an adventure game, Chicory: A Colorful Tale is quite sincerely up there with the very best of the genre.
There’s plenty to see and do and a full completion run will probably take you 25-30 hours. The characters and their travails are rich and likeable, the game’s sense of humour is generally inspired, and it’s all very sweet without being sugary-twee and talking down to the player. It’s also an affecting little tearjerker that will definitely strike a chord if you make art, and almost certainly will even if you don’t – so long as you’re capable of pretty basic empathy.
Chicory is simple to play but impressively long and complex, with perfect controls, performance and visuals. Throw yourself into painting the world and you’ll be left with a game that’s very much your own and speaks to you directly – a beautiful marriage of mechanics, themes and visuals.
While it’s a shame that there are fewer games here than in other Konami collections — we’d have loved to have seen NES title Contra Force or the now-extinct WiiWare title Contra ReBirth — the ones included in the Contra Anniversary Collection are universally brilliant. The 8-bit and 16-bit Contra games are among the finest examples of the run ‘n gun genre, and to have almost all of them included in a single release and emulated flawlessly is an absolute treat.
Whether you’re a fan of the series or a curious onlooker who’s always wanted to see what the fuss was all about, this is essential.
We really like Crawl , and we’d bet our collected stash of gold and wrath you will, too. A dungeon-crawling hack-and-slash affair with roguelike elements, one player is the hero trying to get through a dungeon and the others play as monster-controlling ghosts attempting to kill said hero and take their place.
It's an everyone-for-themselves free-for-all, yet there are opportunities for frantic 3v1 co-operative play — a necessity when all the non-hero ghost characters must take joint control of bosses the hero faces. It’s great fun in single-player thanks to some aggressive AI, but that consistent danger takes on a new dimension when you and three of your friends are jostling for XP and that all-important killing blow.
Competitive couchplay doesn’t get much better than this on Switch.
In 2023, a year dominated by titanic, big-budget releases like Tears of the Kingdom and Mario Wonder , off-the-wall roguelike Dave The Diver stepped up to the plate and knocked the ball clear of the park with a heaving swing.
Its charming animations and writing supplement a mechanically dense experience that never stops dangling a new carrot to chase. You owe it to yourself to pick up this outstandingly funny, enthralling, and weird gem.
Death's Door is a modern classic, utilising old gameplay ideas in a new setting to make for a short and sweet experience you won’t want to miss. The snappy combat, rewarding exploration, and relaxing music will stick with you once you've finished, and while it may not have anything 'new' to offer, Death’s Door is so high quality that you’ll hardly have time to think about its lack of innovation.
Any fans of Zelda or Soulslike games will adore this - Acid Nerve has crafted an experience that’s absolutely worth your time and money.
An attractive art style, strong combat system, and meaningful player choices make Dicefolk a brilliant addition to the library, as it manages to feel fresh without getting too far away from the core ideas that make these sorts of games so addictive and popular.
Dicefolk is a good entry point to the genre, in fact; approachable without being patronising and it’s tons of fun once you get a grasp of it

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Mortgage rates fell this week for the first time since late August, easing some of the pressure on prospective homebuyers facing higher borrowing costs on home loans.
The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.32% from 7.40% last week, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday. One year ago, the average rate was 6.19%.
Borrowing costs on 15-year fixed-rate mortgages, often sought by borrowers refinancing a home loan, also eased this week. That average rate slipped to 6.68% from 6.71% last week. A year ago, it was at 5.44%.
Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors' expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans.
Mortgage rates have been climbing since late February, when the U.S. war with Iran began , pushing up the price of oil and driving inflation higher . The run-up in rates also reflects heightened bond market volatility, which has pushed up yields on U.S. Treasurys.
The 10-year Treasury yield has been mostly easing the last couple of weeks after climbing to its highest level since 2002. That's caused the average rate on a 30-year mortgage to hold steady after reaching 7.4%, its highest level in nearly three years.
The yield was at 5% at midday on the bond market Thursday. It surged to more than 5.30% earlier this month and remains well above its 3.97% level from before the war with Iran.
U.S. home sales remain stalled this year in large part because of rising mortgage rates, which can add hundreds of dollars a month in costs for borrowers, limiting homebuyers' purchasing power and prompting many to put off buying a home.
In late February, the average rate on a 30-year mortgage briefly dipped to 5.98%, its lowest level going back to late 2022. The rise in rates since then has added roughly $355 to the monthly cost for a borrower financing a $400,000 home loan, going by the latest average rate.
Depending on a borrower's income, credit and other factors, they may qualify for a rate on a 30-year mortgage that is below or above the current average.
The U.S. housing market has been in a slump since 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low.
In its latest forecast, mortgage buyer Fannie Mae projects that the rate on a 30-year mortgage will average 7.4% in the final quarter of this year, and average 7.5% in 2027.

PepsiCo and Taco Bell renewed their long-running partnership through 2036, the food and beverage company said on Thursday.
The announcement comes one week after Taco Bell's sister chain KFC said that it will switch to Coca-Cola as its U.S. beverage supplier. While it is unusual for large restaurant chains to switch drink providers, the move is not unprecedented, as Coke and Pepsi try to win contracts through perks and other inducements.
Coke's win over Pepsi was more symbolic, representing another example of how the Atlanta-based company has been beating its rival in the soda category.
Pepsi's relationship with Taco Bell and KFC parent Yum Brands spans decades, back to when the beverage giant owned the restaurant chains before spinning them into a separate public company in 1997. Despite KFC's defection in the U.S., Pepsi remains an important partner for Yum and the chain's international markets, KFC U.S. President Catherine Tan-Gillespie wrote in a memo on Oct. 15 that was obtained by CNBC.
Thanks to its partnership with Pepsi, Taco Bell has long served exclusive menu items that use Pepsi products, like Mountain Dew Baja Blast and Doritos Locos Tacos, at its restaurants.
The renewed deal also means that Taco Bell international markets such as Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Thailand will serve Pepsi products.

articles.title_orig: Four advantages MacBook Pro redesign will have over current model
articles.title_zh: Four advantages MacBook Pro redesign will have over current model
articles.content_orig:
Next week Apple will unveil its first MacBook Pro redesign in five years. Rumors indicate the new MacBook Pro will have the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as current models, but with exclusive advantages in at least four other areas.
While the new MacBook Pro design is expected to be a little thinner than the current model, its biggest design advantage is a weight reduction. Per Mark Gurman :
The new MacBook Pros are lighter — significantly lighter. Apple has reengineered the machine’s interior miniaturizing parts and rearranging components to make the computer much easier to carry.
If you’re worried about Apple removing ports with its MacBook Pro redesign, it sounds like the company probably learned its lesson from previous generations. Since the design isn’t expected to slim down too much, it’s likely there will be minimal changes to ports.
The Liquid Retina XDR display on current MacBook Pros is an excellent display. But Apple plans to make its new MacBook Pro display even better by introducing OLED.
OLED has been used in iPhones for years, but the only example of Apple using it on larger displays is the iPad Pro. The tandem OLED introduced on iPad in 2024 was touted by Apple as “the world’s most advanced display.”
Now, OLED is coming to the Mac with the new MacBook Pro. And if it’s anything like what the iPad Pro offers, the new display is bound to impress.
Most MacBook Pro users probably aren’t asking for touch support. But if you’re like me, you may find that there are some cases where it would be valuable if you could touch the Mac’s display.
Apple’s new MacBook Pro will make that possible. Its OLED display will include full touchscreen capabilities and benefit from touch optimizations throughout macOS Golden Gate.
Touch isn’t replacing the primary input methods of trackpad and keyboard. Rather, it’s being introduced as a secondary “nice-to-have” option.
Apple’s last MacBook Pro redesign in 2021 brought the notch to the Mac. And this redesign will reportedly remove it.
Like Apple has done on the iPhone, it’s removing the notch first on its Pro line. The new MacBook Pro drops the notch, reportedly in favor of a hole-punch camera cutout.
A new Dynamic Island feature is expected to be introduced too, though there’s a chance it might come to older Macs via a software update.

articles.title_orig: Amex Platinum adds Airbnb perks and credits, ends one-night hotel credits
articles.title_zh: Amex Platinum adds Airbnb perks and credits, ends one-night hotel credits
articles.content_orig:
Card benefits are always evolving, and today, it's American Express's turn to announce some changes to one of the big benefits on the American Express Platinum Card® and The Business Platinum Card® from American Express .
Most of the changes are good news, though one may disappoint cardmembers who enjoy using their statement credits for one-night hotel stays.
Let's start with the good news: Amex is adding more than 1 million Airbnb listings to its American Express Travel® booking platform and expanding the Platinum card's newly renamed up to $600 annual lodging statement credit to include select Airbnb Luxe stays. There's also a new up to $250 Airbnb Experiences statement credit you can potentially unlock with those stays.
Here's what you need to know.
Find out your Amex Platinum Card offer: New cardmembers can find out their offer and see if they are eligible for as high as 175,000 bonus points after spending $12,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. (Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.)
Eligible cardmembers can now earn American Express Membership Rewards points on prepaid Airbnb stays booked through Amex Travel or the Amex Travel App™.
Platinum or Business Platinum cardmembers will earn 5 points per dollar spent on eligible bookings, including both Airbnb Luxe and non-Luxe properties.
Based on TPG's October 2026 valuations that value Membership Rewards points at 2 cents each, that's a 10% return on spending in the form of Membership Rewards points, which is pretty solid.
Most other eligible Membership Rewards cards will earn 2 points per dollar spent on prepaid Airbnb bookings through Amex Travel or the Amex Travel App.
And while earning bonus points is always nice, being able to use statement credits is even better. That's where two additional changes to the Platinum's benefits come into play.
The Amex Platinum's up to $600 annual lodging statement credit (formerly the $600 hotel statement credit) is split into two up to $300 biannual statement credits — one from January through June and the other from July through December.
The statement credit can now be used toward eligible prepaid Airbnb Luxe stays booked through Amex Travel or the Amex Travel App, in addition to qualifying Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection bookings.
To use one of these up to $300 statement credits on an Airbnb stay, you'll need to book through Amex Travel and stay at least two nights and select a property that's part of Airbnb Luxe.
Airbnb describes its Luxe properties as "private homes in sought-after destinations around the world, each selected by Airbnb for its quality, design and distinctive setting."
In my test searches, Luxe properties made up only a small subset of Airbnb listings. But there are certainly some options where a $300 statement credit could go a long way toward a two-night stay, including this example I found in Gatlinburg, Tennessee, where two nights later this year cost $874.
Assuming the booking meets the statement credit's eligibility requirements, the stay could drop to just $574 for two nights at a pretty great-looking spot with three bedrooms in the Smokies.
If you book an eligible prepaid Airbnb Luxe stay through Amex Travel using your Platinum or Business Platinum Card, you'll unlock access to an all-new up to $250 annual statement credit for eligible Airbnb Experiences, whether or not you use your lodging credit toward the stay.
This additional credit can be unlocked once per calendar year and is valid for the remainder of that year. Unlike the lodging credit, Airbnb Experiences can be booked directly through Airbnb.
In my searches, Airbnb Experiences cover a wide range of activities, including paddleboarding, airboat rides, sunset cruises, walking tours, food tours and cultural experiences.
Prices for some experiences start around $10 to $20, while private tours and other higher-end activities can cost several hundred dollars. In other words, $250 could go a long way towards an experience.
There's also some flexibility here: Your Airbnb Experience doesn't need to take place during your Luxe stay or even in the same destination. It can happen before or after your stay, and even in a future calendar year, as long as you purchase it after your Luxe booking is confirmed and before the end of the calendar year.
There's no minimum spending requirement for an eligible Airbnb Experience, so you can use the credit toward smaller purchases or an eligible Experience costing $250 or more.
For 2026, that means cardmembers who book a qualifying prepaid Airbnb Luxe stay now can unlock up to $250 in statement credits for eligible Airbnb Experiences purchased by Dec. 31 — even if the experience itself takes place in 2027.
More ways to use existing credits and new credits to unlock are certainly good news.
But as Amex expands the ways to use the Platinum's newly renamed $600 annual lodging statement credit, it's also making a change that won't be welcome news for everyone.
Previously, stays booked through The Hotel Collection ( which I recently tried and loved ) required at least two nights to use the Platinum's lodging credit. However, Fine Hotels + Resorts stays had no minimum stay requirement, meaning you could use an up to $300 credit toward a stay of just one night.
Beginning Jan. 1, 2027, all eligible uses of the Platinum's lodging statement credit will require stays of at least two nights, whether you're booking through Fine Hotels + Resorts, The Hotel Collection or Airbnb Luxe. You can still get Fine Hotels + Resorts benefits on one-night stays, just not utilize the lodging credit.
This creates a consistent requirement across all three booking options, but it's still probably disappointing news for cardholders who have enjoyed using their credits toward one-night Fine Hotels + Resorts stays.
The good news is that if you still have one of this year's up to $300 statement credits burning a hole in your pocket, you can still use it toward an eligible one-night Fine Hotels + Resorts stay before the new requirement takes effect in 2027.
Related: How I used my Fine Hotels + Resorts credit and came out $1 ahead
If you use the major credits and benefits, it's possible to get substantially more value from the American Express Platinum and Business Platinum Cards each year than you pay in annual fees.
But the key to doing that is taking advantage of major credits and benefits like the newly renamed $600 annual lodging statement credit — and potentially even unlocking another $250 in Airbnb Experiences statement credits.
Having more ways to use those credits is certainly welcome news. However, cardholders who have gotten used to using their credits for one-night Fine Hotels + Resorts stays will, unfortunately, need a new strategy beginning next year.
Let us know in the comments how these changes impact your strategy and what you think of the new Airbnb Luxe and Experiences options.

articles.title_orig: Iran says 7 oil tankers attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as fears grow of a return to war
articles.title_zh: Iran says 7 oil tankers attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as fears grow of a return to war
articles.content_orig:
Iran says that seven oil tankers have been struck and sustained damage in the Strait of Hormuz, the largest single-day toll for the waterway since the United States and Israel started their war against Iran on February 28.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said in a statement on Thursday that four of the vessels were transferring oil when they were targeted and caught fire overnight. The other three were disabled after striking mines.
The claims could not be independently verified, and the report did not provide details about possible casualties or the tankers’ flags.
The IRGC also warned that it could strike US bases across the Middle East if Washington moves to help tankers transit other parts of the strait.
“The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the IRGC said in a statement on its Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning.”
Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.
But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks.
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that “Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil prior to the US Midterm Election”.
In a post on his Truth Social platform, he added: “They are making up fake hits, mines, and everything else because more oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the conflict.”
A US Central Command spokesperson, speaking anonymously to Al Jazeera, also called Iran’s mine claims incorrect.
The spokesperson said US forces have cleared the international shipping lanes of mines and that Iran is using missiles and drones.
The strait remains open, the spokesperson said, with 95 percent of vessels getting through.
The attacks, the spokesperson added, show Tehran’s “desperation” under the US blockade, which cuts Iran off from the resources it needs to rebuild the military capabilities the US has said it destroyed.
“The number of ships and tankers attacked every single day is increasing, and Iran is saying it is continuing to do this because they are not going to allow any change in that situation,” said Al Jazeera’s Mohamed Vall, reporting from Tehran.
“They have full control over the Strait of Hormuz right now, they say.”
Vall said there is also talk in Tehran about an imminent escalation in the war, with the Iranians expecting the US to attack even before US midterm elections in early November.
“The IRGC army chief has boasted that Iran is more ready than anytime before, and has produced enough weapons and equipment to wage a symmetrical war against the United States,” he said.
Reporting from the US White House, Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett said: “Striking Iran does not appear to serve any Republican interests”, adding that pre-election polls tell the same story for Trump’s political party.
“What we’ve seen in surveys in recent months, and as of today, is that most Americans want relief from their tax money going to pay for any potential war with Iran that is ramped up,” Halkett said.
“There is real frustration over the rising cost for everyday Americans, given the rising fuel prices that have occurred as a result of this conflict  … As a result, the US president is having to make the case.
“The pressure is on the president, and it’s not just from the opposition party,” she said. “It is also from within the Republican Party as well.”
